tier_reason: The README compares banzai with the bzip2 reference implementation only qualitatively (similar compression ratios, worse average runtime, better worst-case runtime) and gives no measurements; the repo tree (bnz, debug, fuzz, lib) holds no benchmark code or results.
notes: The record is accurate: the README quotes, the MIT license, 30 stars, crates.io 0.3.2 with 28,436 downloads, and the 2026-07-28 edition-bump commit (previous commit 2022-09-26) all check out. Shortcoming: not faster than the C baseline. The author says the average runtime is worse than bzip2, the only advantage is the SA-IS worst case on pathological inputs, the build is encoder-only, and there are no numbers. 'Active' rests only on a Rust-edition bump; the code has been unchanged since 2022.

tier_reason: The README benchmark (go test -bench BenchmarkRealDataFastOr, Threadripper 2950X, numbers matching the record) compares sroar only with the Go RoaringBitmap/roaring roaring64 library; neither this fork nor the dgraph-io upstream has any CRoaring or other C/C++ measurement, so there are no numbers against the wave's C/C++ baseline.

corrections.caveats: Recorded at D: the lead said to record only a CRoaring comparison and none exists; the numbers above are against the Go library, not a C or C++ baseline. This URL is a fork of the archived upstream dgraph-io/sroar (archived 2024-07-18, 277 stars, 47 forks, same 84 commits; the fork's last commit is 2022-05-27), and go.mod still declares module github.com/dgraph-io/sroar, so the canonical record should probably use the dgraph-io URL. Raw benchmark outputs are in benchmarks/; the README names the CPU (AMD Ryzen Threadripper 2950X 16-Core) but not the Go version. FastOr only, not And or other operations, and run containers are not implemented. The 6.5x median figure covers only benchmarks over 1 ms and hides three slowdowns (weather_sept_85 +78.52%, uscensus2000 +42.17%, census-income_srt +279.09%); memory use also rises on dimension_033, uscensus2000 and weather_sept_85.

notes: README numbers and metadata are accurate: Apache-2.0, 0 stars, a fork of dgraph-io/sroar, last commit 2022-05-27, and the census1881, wikileaks-noquotes and dimension_033 rows all match. Shortcoming: off-baseline. There is no C or C++ comparison, only Go roaring64, and the win comes from a serialized, allocation-free layout rather than from the language. Consider a repo_url override to https://github.com/dgraph-io/sroar (the canonical upstream, archived 2024-07-18), which is not yet in the catalog. I dropped the 'author's desktop' wording from the caveats because the README does not say that.
